question: How much of the continuous-ECG performance gap is explained by allowing validation subjects to appear in training while keeping records disjoint?
paper_role: Protocol-sensitivity diagnostic; never a strict-LOSO result and never the main REM-Net claim
hard_guards: train and validation record_id sets are disjoint
validation subject overlap with training is measured and reported
full 8-second WSST support is generated from each source H5
checkpoint selection uses validation composite only
Shape-200 is auxiliary and excluded from checkpoint selection
model: B1 continuous model, identical executable path, loss, 80/20 budget, evaluator and seed policy to the repaired loso_v2 B1 pilot
comparison: Against repaired loso_v2 B1 validation results on folds 1/5/9; protocol labels remain separate because the subject units differ

decision_rule.protocol_effect_supported: subject-overlap PCC exceeds repaired strict-LOSO fold-macro B1 PCC by at least 0.15 without worse R2
decision_rule.otherwise: do not explain the literature gap primarily by subject reuse; retain model/task mismatch as a major cause

prohibited_claims: calling this sample-wise unless window allocation is actually used
mixing this number into the strict-LOSO aggregate
using the unopened test partition for selection or reporting
